key_insight: Conformal prediction turns neural-operator CFD surrogates from deterministic predictors into calibrated aerodynamic reliability indicators at both vehicle and surface levels.
engineering_relevance: This enables engineers to identify which vehicle geometries and surface regions need extra CFD verification, improving surrogate use in design iteration.
method: Use GeoTransolver as the main neural-operator backbone and compare transfer with Transolver.
Build case-level drag intervals with conformalized quantile regression.
For pressure and WSS, combine point prediction with residual-scale estimation and residual-normalized conformal calibration, then compare global, point-adaptive, and case-wise protocols.
evidence_signal: On the DrivAerML dataset with 90% nominal coverage, out-of-fold calibration reduced drag coverage variability from 10.41 to 3.10 percentage points and cut surface-field interval widths by up to 27.09% while keeping near-nominal coverage.
watch_item: Case-wise normalized intervals improve reliability but are more conservative, so the chosen calibration protocol must balance width, coverage, and deployment cost.
paper_title: Multi-Granularity Conformal Prediction for Reliable Neural-Operator Automotive Aerodynamic Surrogates
